title: Budget Billing Plans Held Across a Customer's Service Agreements
content:
# Budget Billing Plans Held Across a Customer's Service Agreements

**Rule.** A customer may hold Budget Billing plans on several service agreements, one per service agreement. No other plan on the same service agreement is in enrolled or active status. Moving from one plan kind to another requires withdrawing from the first.

There is no limit on the number of the customer's service agreements that may each carry a plan; the limit is one open plan on each agreement.

## What the rule turns on

| Element | Reading |
|---|---|
| Object | The individual Electric Service Agreement on which the enrollment is made |
| Plans that count | Any Budget Billing plan on that same agreement whose status is enrolled (accepted, first plan bill not yet issued) or active |
| Plans that do not count | Plans on the same agreement that are withdrawn, removed or closed; plans on the customer's other agreements |
| Authority | The company's plan records for that agreement, as they stand before the enrollment is made |

## Condition, judgement and result

- **Condition:** a new enrollment is requested on a service agreement.
- **Judgement:** do the company's records show another Budget Billing plan on that same agreement in enrolled or active status?
- **Result:** where none is shown, the agreement is open to a plan under this rule. Where one is shown, the new enrollment is not accepted on that agreement; a change from one plan kind to another on it requires withdrawing from the first plan.

## Illustrations (hypothetical customers)

- A business customer with three sites holds the Commercial Levelized Billing Plan at two of them and asks for a plan at the third, which carries none. The third agreement carries no enrolled or active plan, so this rule does not stand in the way.
- A residential customer on the Residential Budget Billing Plan, active, asks to be put on the Residential Levelized Billing Plan on the same agreement. The active plan is an open plan on that agreement; moving to the other plan kind requires withdrawing from the Residential Budget Billing Plan first.
- An agreement whose only Budget Billing record is a Residential Levelized Billing Plan in withdrawn status carries no plan in enrolled or active status, so this rule does not stand in the way of a new enrollment there.
